author: Scott Kolb Sports reporter scott@codyenterprise.com
title: Meeteetse relay team close to new school record | Sports | codyenterprise.com
text:
Chasing a school record in the 4 x 100 meters relay gave the Meeteetse boys a state qualifying time in last week’s Bobcat Invitational.
This meet took place last Friday in Thermopolis. Worland had the top team finish for the girls, and the host team from Thermopolis won the boys meet.
The Meeteetse Longhorns relay team of Jacob Moody, Will Hatch, Max Potas and Remington Harris set down a state qualifying time of 46.7 seconds. This gave them a top 10 finish in the event.
“These boys have been chasing the school record for the last couple of years,” Meeteetse coach Molly Potas said. “They’re just three-tenths of a second off breaking that 2021 school record. We have a goal for state this year.”
Harris also qualified for the Class 1A State Meet with a time of 11.79 seconds in the 100 meters. Moody, Jon Duncan and Darius Mickelson also ran in this event at the Bobcat Invite.
Many of the Meeteetse boys and girls set new personal records in various events at the meet. Anna Hohnhorst had a top 20 finish in the 100 hurdles. Kaydence Christopherson was among the top 15 finishers in the triple jump. Harris had a top 20 finish in the 200 meters and placed 10th in the pole vault.
“We are excited for regional track in Shoshoni this weekend,” coach Potas added. “We have many athletes teetering right on the line of qualifying for state, so we should see a push over that line and continue building that state roster.”
The Class 1A and 2A West Regional Meet takes place on Friday and Saturday. In addition to qualifying times, this meet serves as a qualifier for the state championships with the top eight individuals and top four relay teams advancing to the next level.
